title: Shedeur Sanders Lost The Browns QB Battle-But This Is Far From Over - NewsBreak
text:
By oumardinhussen ,
15 minutes ago The Cleveland Browns have made their quarterback decision for Week 1, and Shedeur Sanders will begin the 2026 season behind Deshaun Watson.
For Sanders, it is a disappointing outcome after a preseason in which he completed a higher percentage of his passes than Watson. But Cleveland’s decision does not necessarily close the door on his future. In fact, the next few months could be just as important for Sanders as the quarterback competition itself.
Head coach Todd Monken has made it clear that Watson is the starter and that the decision is not expected to become a week-to-week debate. At the same time, Monken has praised Sanders’ development and said the Browns are excited about his future. That leaves Sanders with a simple but important job: stay ready.
Why Shedeur Sanders Lost The Browns QB Battle Aug 22, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images The numbers alone do not completely explain Cleveland’s decision. Through two preseason appearances, Watson completed 16 of 27 passes for 162 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. Sanders completed 15 of 22 attempts for 153 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. That gave Sanders a 68.2% completion rate compared with Watson’s 59.3%.
Sanders also had a strong showing against the Buffalo Bills. He completed 9 of 11 passes for 74 yards and a touchdown, although he also threw an interception during Cleveland’s 31-7 loss. Watson, playing with Cleveland’s reserves, completed only 5 of 12 passes for 35 yards and threw an interception.
On paper, that could make Sanders look like the obvious choice. But Monken repeatedly emphasized that the decision would be based on the quarterbacks’ full body of work, including training camp practices and preseason performances. Experience ultimately gave Watson the advantage.
Sanders Still Gave The Browns Plenty To Like Jul 30, 2026; Berea, OH, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) talks with his father Deion Sanders during training camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Losing the competition does not mean Sanders played poorly. Monken praised Sanders after his performance against Buffalo, pointing to his confidence and improvement in getting rid of the football. The second-year quarterback also showed that he could operate Cleveland’s offense efficiently when given the opportunity.
That matters because Sanders is still developing. The Browns do not need him to prove everything immediately; they need him to continue improving until another opportunity arrives. And that opportunity could come sooner than expected.
NFL seasons rarely go exactly according to plan at quarterback. Injuries, poor performance, and unexpected changes can quickly turn a backup into the most important player on a roster. Sanders needs to be prepared for that possibility.
Deshaun Watson’s Performance Will Decide Sanders’ Opportunity The biggest factor in Sanders’ future may have nothing to do with Sanders himself. It will be Watson.
Cleveland has committed to Watson as its Week 1 starter, and Monken has specifically said the decision is not a week-to-week arrangement. That means Sanders should not expect to enter the lineup simply because Watson has one bad game.
But Watson also enters 2026 with significant questions. He missed the entire 2025 season after suffering Achilles injuries and has dealt with injuries and limited availability since joining Cleveland. The Browns are now counting on him to stay healthy and perform well enough to justify the decision to make him their starter.
If Watson performs well, Sanders may spend most of the season learning from the sideline. If Watson struggles badly, however, the conversation could change quickly. That is why Sanders’ development remains so important.
Sanders Should Not Treat This As A Setback Aug 15, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) prepares to run a play against the Chicago Bears during the first half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images It is easy to look at losing a quarterback competition as a failure. For Sanders, that would be the wrong approach. He now knows exactly where he stands.
Watson is QB1. Sanders has to prepare as though he could be needed at any moment. That clarity can actually help a young quarterback.
Instead of worrying about winning the job every day, Sanders can focus on improving specific areas of his game: processing defenses, throwing with anticipation, protecting the football, and becoming more consistent under pressure. The Browns already know what Sanders can do when things go well. Now they need to see how much he can improve when things do not.
The Preseason Numbers Were Not Enough To Win The Job Sanders’ completion percentage was better than Watson’s, but completion percentage alone cannot determine a quarterback competition. The Browns were evaluating much more than box-score statistics. They were watching practices, decision-making, command of the offense, communication, consistency, and how each quarterback handled different situations.
That is why Sanders’ stronger completion percentage did not automatically make him the winner. It also explains why Cleveland can believe in Sanders’ future while still choosing Watson for Week 1. Those two decisions are not contradictory.
The Browns can believe Watson gives them the best chance to win immediately while also believing Sanders could become important later.
Sanders’ Best Move Is To Stay Ready For Sanders, the next stage is about preparation. He cannot control when Cleveland might need him, but he can control whether he is ready when that moment arrives. That means treating every practice rep seriously and continuing to learn the offense.
It also means learning from Watson. Regardless of the debate surrounding the Browns’ decision , Watson has considerably more NFL experience, and Sanders can use that experience as a resource while continuing to develop his own game.
The goal should not be to sit around waiting for Watson to fail. The goal should be to make sure that if the Browns eventually call his number, there is no question that Sanders is prepared.
Cleveland May Still Need Sanders This Season Aug 22, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) scrambles during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images The Browns have not eliminated Sanders from their plans. They have simply chosen Watson to start. That distinction is important.
Cleveland’s season will begin with Watson against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13. The Browns then face Tampa Bay before returning home to play Carolina in Week 3. Those early games will provide a significant test for Watson.
If Watson stays healthy and performs well, the Browns will have little reason to make a change. But if the offense struggles or Watson’s health becomes an issue, Sanders could suddenly become one of the most important players on the roster. That is the nature of being a backup quarterback in the NFL.
Sanders’ Long-Term Future Is Still Unclear There is another reason this season matters for Sanders. The Browns eventually need to determine whether he can become more than a backup.
The Browns drafted Sanders in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, and he gained regular-season experience during his rookie season after initially beginning the year as a backup. Now he has another season to develop.
If Sanders gets an opportunity and performs well, Cleveland could eventually face a much bigger quarterback decision. Does Watson remain the long-term answer? Can Sanders develop into a legitimate starter? Or does Cleveland eventually decide that neither quarterback is the answer?
Those questions do not need to be answered today, but Sanders’ performance whenever he gets his next opportunity could influence all of them.
End Of My Shedeur Sanders Rant Shedeur Sanders lost the Browns’ quarterback competition to Deshaun Watson. That part is settled. But the bigger question is what Sanders does next.
The Browns saw enough during training camp and preseason to remain excited about his development, even though Watson ultimately won the starting job.
For Sanders, the path forward is straightforward. Keep improving. Protect the football. Learn from Watson. Stay ready. And when the opportunity comes, make it impossible for Cleveland to ignore him.
The quarterback competition may be over for Week 1, but Sanders’ story in Cleveland is far from finished. The Browns chose Watson for now. What happens next could determine whether that decision lasts all season.
